subject: Re: Surge impact – 429 retry amplification causing p99/timeouts
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena@fastpay.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: Intermittent timeouts + 429 spike affecting checkout (URGENT)

Hi Laura,

We started seeing elevated checkout latency and a spike in 429s starting ~08:50 UTC. Our SREs report a run of client-side retries that quickly drove p99 above 3s and caused a handful of timeouts that translated to checkout failures. This is impacting a small percent of customers but it’s happening on every region.

Attached are a small sample of our logs (fastpay-retry-sample.log) and a stack of traces. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a known rollover/maintenance or an unexpected surge? We need an ETA and a mitigation plan — we may need throttling advice on our side.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure, FastPay

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T09:31:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent timeouts + 429 spike affecting checkout (URGENT)

Forwarding FastPay report — initial triage below.

---
Marcus Lin (SRE) initial notes:
- Observed hosted-api p95/p99 increase around 08:48–09:05 UTC across both dc-us-west-2 and dc-us-east-1.
- Large proportion of 429s correlate with short-lived rate-limiter events on a subset of replica pools hosting smaller models.
- Customer retry policy: exponential backoff but short initial delay (100ms) and max 6 tries — this can amplify when many clients retry simultaneously.
- Hypothesis: a transient capacity dip on certain pools triggered per-key rate limiting; upstream retries amplified queueing and KV cache misses, raising tail latency.

Immediate triage actions started:
1) Temporarily raise soft rate limit threshold for FastPay customer route to reduce 429 returns (risk: higher CPU).
2) Route FastPay traffic to a less-congested model variant (same version, higher concurrency).
3) Engage runtime team to examine batching windows for affected pools.

I can enact 1+2 now; need approval from Rishi for routing changes that impact capacity accounting.

Marcus
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent timeouts + 429 spike affecting checkout (URGENT)

Do the temporary mitigations. Prioritize avoiding customer-facing errors.

Actions approved:
- Marcus: increase soft limit for customer route FP-73 by 25% for the next 45 minutes.
- Marcus/Grace: perform a targeted route move of 10% of FastPay traffic to dedicated high-concurrency pool; monitor p95/p99 and CPU.
- Monica: push a one-line advisory to FastPay SRE telling them to lengthen initial backoff to 300ms and cap retries at 4 while we stabilize.

We’ll capture a post-incident note. Keep execs updated if there is any SLA exposure.
Rishi

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: execs@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T18:02:00Z
Subject: Executive brief — FastPay 429/retry amplification incident (summary)

Team,

Summary: Today ~08:48–09:10 UTC we observed a transient p95/p99 regression for a subset of hosted-api pools impacting FastPay (deal FP-2026-REDWOOD-73). The root cause appears to be a short capacity dip in replica pools + conservative per-key rate limiting. FastPay’s aggressive client retry policy (100ms initial, up to 6 tries) amplified the failure surface and raised queueing/KV cache churn. Result: some checkout timeouts and customer-visible errors (~0.6% of sessions during window).

Mitigations performed:
- Temporarily raised soft-per-key limits for FastPay route (+25% for 45 minutes).
- Shifted 10% of traffic to higher-concurrency pool.
- Suggested retry tuning to FastPay (initial backoff 300ms, max 4 tries).

Current status: stabilized; p99 in affected flows reduced to ~1.2s and error rates returned to baseline. No SLA credits expected at this time; we will confirm with legal/sales once we complete postmortem.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Rishi/Marcus: postmortem checklist and capacity hardening recommendations (due 2027-04-04).
- Runtime: evaluate rate limiter smoothing and short-window suppression logic.
- Sales/CS: update FastPay with post-incident note and confirm retry change.

I recommend we add a short runbook entry for per-tenant rate-limit escalation and a conservative default retry guidance document for customers.

Laura Bennett
Account Exec (Sales), Redwood Inference
cc: Grace O’Connor (Product), Legal for potential SLA review
